note: The strict rerun rule's script, scripts/mutants-due.py. Each mutant switches off one path by which a change makes a mutant file due; the judges are the self-test and the three real runs against this tree -- a header between a mutant and its tests (core/Scalar.hpp, which must make m1-12 and m1-87 due, the second only through its headers), a shader no mutant touches (which must make m1-13 due through its application judge), and a script on a ctest command line (which must make m1-15 due). A Python mutant needs no build, but the harness always builds, so every mutant names orbsim_shaders as a no-op. Not mutated: the line that adds each mutated file to its own inputs, because every mutated file here is also reached another way -- its judges are built from it, or read it at run time, or it is in the always-due set -- so removing that line changes no verdict in this repository; and mutate.py's record_pass, which only the harness itself exercises, checked by hand instead (a pass over an uncommitted tree must say 'pass not recorded'). **First run, 2026-09-27: 5 caught, 2 survived.** 'An expected file that is not due is not reported' was a real hole -- every real run expected a file that is due -- closed by mutants_due_unmet_expectation_fails, which must fail. 'Shaders are no longer an input' is equivalent here and declared, on the owner's ruling (decision 218).
